source.title: From Directions to Regions: Decomposing Activations in Language Models via Local Geometry
source.authors: O. Shafran; S. Ronen; Omri Fahn; Shauli Ravfogel; Atticus Geiger; Mor Geva

record.tranche_reason: Applies a new local-geometry decomposition to Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-2-2B and reports results on their activation representations; it does not reproduce the toy-model method.
record.gate_note: Included the paper’s measurements and explicit findings about local subspaces and neighboring Gaussian components. Localization benchmark scores do not themselves measure the claim versions, and steering deliberately induces concepts, so those results are not rows for these versions. The paper’s broader prose and cited prior work are not treated as new measurements.
record.test_reason: This is mainly a method paper, using Mixtures of Factor Analyzers (MFA) on Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-2-2B. Its only direct result on a claim version is a measurement on Gemmascope/Llamascope SAE decompositions: about 0.29 of an SAE decomposition's contribution is interpretable in context, and 75% of active features are not directly interpretable. The authors use this to argue that SAE directions are not good units, which bears on V5. The MFA geometry results (broad/narrow regions, neighbouring Gaussians sharing themes) describe MFA components, not the dimensionality of superposed features, so they do not test V6 or V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that MFA outperforms unsupervised baselines on localization, is competitive with supervised methods, and steers better than SAEs. They present local subspaces as a promising unit of analysis, not as a refutation of direction-based or superposition accounts.
record.recipe_differences: Uses large-scale Mixtures of Factor Analyzers on LLM residual-stream activations, rather than training small synthetic networks and measuring sparse-feature superposition.
record.method_sensitivity: The broad/narrow region balance and semantic/syntactic loading frequencies vary with K and model family: Gemma shifts more toward narrow regions as K increases, whereas Llama remains predominantly broad at K=32,000.

fits_no_version.finding: MFA Gaussians split into broad (semantic) and narrow (token-level) regions, with model-dependent shares. 61%/36%/20% of 8K-MFA components have ≥1/≥2/3 same-theme nearest neighbours.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLM activation space is organised into local low-rank regions, and concepts span neighbouring regions.

fits_no_version.finding: Restricting MFA to centroids drops MCQA localization from 80% to 39%. A global factor analysis reaches only about 35% versus MFA's 80.2%/70.5%. On RAVEL, centroids alone or a global FA match MFA.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some causal variables live in within-region (local subspace) variation rather than in global directions.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning (PMLR 306, 2026)
record.problems: The local-geometry evidence is based on the paper’s chosen MFA decomposition and annotations, not a controlled test of superposition. Figure 3’s proportions are not given numerically in the text. The semantic-neighbor result is an aggregate across 670 components without model-specific results and uses an LLM judge. The SAE interpretability comparison does not test stability or canonicality.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant rows omitted. Localization benchmark results and steering scores were left out because they do not directly measure the listed claim versions; steering intentionally induces target concepts.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transition or feature geometry under capacity pressure.
No neuron-level polysemanticity or importance/capacity allocation.
No test of non-capacity causes of polysemanticity.
Does not measure how features spread across neurons. SAE reconstruction (Appendix D) appears only as a comparator to MFA.
Stability across seeds/data, completeness and canonicality of SAE features are not tested; only contextual interpretability is.
No controlled comparison of 1-D versus multi-dimensional feature models. The subspace view is assumed by MFA's construction, not tested.

record.verdict_notes: Appendix D shows SAEs achieve lower reconstruction MSE than MFA in all settings; this is a comparator value, not a test of V4. Localization and steering scores are own-method benchmarks and are rightly excluded. The paper never mentions superposition directly. Its stance against isolated global directions is an argument, not a controlled test of V6.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test toy networks, sparse features competing for dimensions, feature overlap/interference, or a sparsity-dependent transition.
Does not test neuron polysemanticity or whether importance and capacity determine which features get dedicated dimensions.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
Does not establish that a complete set of model features is recovered, or measure how features are distributed across individual neurons.
Tests contextual interpretability of SAE decomposition features, but not their stability across data, training, or methods, nor whether they are complete or canonical units.

Findings concern local subspaces and concepts spanning neighboring Gaussian components; the paper does not directly test superposition or compare a one-dimensional feature model against a multi-dimensional one under controlled conditions.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-2-2B (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Annotated MFA components and their loadings across the trained model/layer/scale settings.
rows.measure: Broad versus narrow Gaussian share; semantic versus syntactic loading share
rows.value: Figure only; text states that increasing K increases narrow regions in both models, with Gemma shifting more toward narrow regions while Llama remains predominantly broad even at K=32,000. Text also states that narrow Gaussians skew more syntactic and broad Gaussians more semantic, and that semantic loadings become more frequent as K increases.
rows.note: The paper reports trends in text but does not give the plotted percentages numerically. Annotations use sampled contexts and an automated GPT-5-mini pipeline.
rows.check: Broad/narrow and semantic/syntactic shares of MFA Gaussians describe the paper's own decomposition. They do not measure whether features are 1-D, how features spread over neurons, or whether an SAE recovers sparse features. Values are figure-only.

rows.subject: 8K MFAs (aggregate across models; 670 components)
rows.operation_detail: Measured whether each component’s three nearest centroid neighbors shared its semantic theme, using an LLM judge.

conditions.value: three nearest components by Euclidean centroid distance

rows.measure: Components with at least one same-theme neighbor
rows.note: Aggregate result across the trained 8K MFAs; no model-specific breakdown is stated.
rows.check: Same-theme neighbours among MFA centroids (LLM judge, no baseline or random-neighbour control) say how MFA components cluster. They do not compare 1-D with multi-dimensional features, so the link to V4/V6 is unwarranted.

rows.subject: SAEs (Gemmascope and Llamascope; aggregate across settings)
rows.size_stated: Gemmascope and Llamascope; specific SAE widths not stated for this measurement
rows.operation_detail: Measured the fraction of decomposition contribution assigned to features judged interpretable in context.

conditions.value: 50 activations per method from The Pile

rows.note: The paper also states that, on average, 75% of active SAE features were not directly interpretable from context. This measures contextual interpretability, not feature stability or canonicality.
rows.check: Bears on V5 only through contextual interpretability of SAE features (IF 0.29 ± 0.2). Judging was asymmetric: SAE features were scored by an LLM judge checking Neuronpedia descriptions against context (κ=0.61 with humans), while MFA terms were scored by humans on neighbour placement. The MFA baseline is the study's own method.

rows.subject: MFAs (aggregate across settings)
rows.operation_detail: Measured the fraction of decomposition contribution assigned to features judged interpretable in context.

conditions.value: 50 activations per method from The Pile

rows.note: MFA’s local term was judged as a subspace placement rather than by treating each loading as an isolated feature.
rows.check: This is the study's own method's interpretability score (MFA IF 0.96), a method-performance value rather than a measurement of any version.

relationships.condition: Gemmascope/Llamascope SAE decompositions of Wikipedia/Pile activations, LLM-judged against Neuronpedia descriptions
relationships.reason: R5: SAE IF 0.29 ± 0.2, and 75% of active features are not interpretable in context. This qualifies treating SAE features as the model's units, but the judging protocol was asymmetric with MFA's.
relationships.display_finding: SAE features scored an IF of 0.29 ± 0.2, and 75% of active features were judged not interpretable in context, though the judging protocol differed from the one used for MFA.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
